**Domain regex is too restrictive and may reject valid domains.**

Issues:
1. Doesn't support subdomains (e.g., `www.ogabassey.com`, `shop.example.com`)
2. Requires all-lowercase input but domains are case-insensitive
3. Doesn't allow single-character labels between dots



Apply this diff to support standard domain formats:

```diff
-// Valid domain pattern: basic domain format (e.g., ogabassey.com)
-const VALID_DOMAIN_REGEX = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.[a-z]{2,}$/;
+// Valid domain pattern: supports domains and subdomains (case-insensitive)
+const VALID_DOMAIN_REGEX = /^([a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,}$/i;
```

This pattern:
- Uses the `i` flag for case-insensitive matching
- Supports subdomains (e.g., `www.ogabassey.com`, `shop.store.example.com`)
- Allows single-character labels
- Still prevents trailing/leading hyphens in each label
